title: Electric Cars: The Future of Transport?
content: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are rapidly becoming a common sight on our roads. Governments around the world are encouraging their adoption to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and combat climate change. Unlike traditional petrol cars, EVs produce zero tailpipe emissions and are much quieter. Over the past decade, battery technology has improved significantly, allowing electric cars to travel much further on a single charge than before. However, the transition to electric transport faces hurdles. A major challenge is the lack of charging infrastructure, particularly in rural areas. Additionally, while the cars themselves are emission-free, the electricity used to charge them often comes from fossil fuels. Finally, the mining of materials like lithium and cobalt for the batteries raises environmental and ethical concerns.
